lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eBuenas prácticas: cer:
"

Good practice: close the stopcock before adding; invert and vent (especially with ether and with NaHCO₃, which releases CO₂); shake gently; let it settle; remove the stopper before draining; keep both phases until finished. Dry the organic phase with anhydrous Na₂SO₄ or MgSO₄ and evaporate the solvent.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon el mismo volumen:
"

With the same total volume of organic solvent, several extractions with small portions recover more solute than a single large one. The fraction remaining in the water after n stages is (1/(1 + K·r/n))n. Usually 3 extractions are a good compromise between yield and work.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el equilibrio, el:
"

At equilibrium, the solute is distributed according to the partition coefficient K = Corg/Caq. With volumes Vorg and Vaq, the fraction extracted in one stage is E = K·r/(1 + K·r) with r = Vorg/Vaq. Change K and r and watch how the dots redistribute between the two phases.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eextra:
"

Liquid–liquid extraction transfers a solute from one phase (usually aqueous) to an immiscible organic solvent. The phase of lower density stays on top: ether (0.71) and ethyl acetate (0.90) above water; dichloromethane (1.33) stays below. A separatory funnel is used: shake, vent the pressure and separate the phases.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eácido:
"

A carboxylic acid is neutral (organic-soluble) at pH < pKa and an ionic carboxylate (water-soluble) at pH > pKa. With NaHCO₃ it is extracted into the aqueous phase; on acidifying with HCl it is recovered. With an amine the opposite happens: HCl turns it into an aqueous salt. The effective coefficient is D = K·fneutral. This is how acids, bases and neutral compounds are separated from a mixture.

"
